facts.text: Chauvin takes its name from early French settler families, the Chauvin brothers, who arrived in Louisiana during the 18th century.
West of the village lies the Bayou Chauvin Oil and Gas Field, a reminder of the area's energy history.
Chauvin's most iconic landmark is the Chauvin Sculpture Garden, created by self‑taught artist Kenny Hill between 1988 and 2000.
The town sits on the Terrebonne Basin, an abandoned Mississippi River delta where natural subsidence makes it especially vulnerable to storm surges.
Tourists flock to Chauvin for saltwater fishing charters and boating excursions that showcase the region’s vibrant waterways.
Bayou Petit Caillou, a tidal waterway, meanders through wetlands and connects inland areas to Terrebonne Bay, shaping local hydrology.
